title: Memory × Mathematics × Consciousness
content_html:
Memory × Mathematics × Consciousness

Stabilising Illusions

Human memory is constructive and probabilistic. Reconstruction yields stability for the self but introduces systematic distortions; these are adaptive trade-offs.

  • Reconstruction & distortions (Schacter’s “sins of memory”).
  • Collective memory externalizes stability beyond any one brain (Halbwachs).

Conscious access likely reflects a global broadcasting/ignition mechanism and predictive coding that compresses and stabilizes experience.

  • Global Neuronal Workspace (Dehaene; Mashour et al.).
  • Predictive processing (Clark): cortex minimizes prediction error via hierarchical models.

Symbolic systems externalize stable, recursively composable structures. They powerfully model the world yet face intrinsic limits (incompleteness) and live debates about ontological status (e.g., Mathematical Universe Hypothesis).

  • Gödel’s incompleteness limits formal certainty.
  • Tegmark’s MUH and critiques explore whether reality “is” mathematics.

All three act as stabilizing illusions — functional fictions that compress complexity into persistent forms we can share, test, and refine.
